section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar.
section.t: The second day of Rosh HaShanah,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section notes that the text is a transcription of an oral discourse.
This section explains that Rosh HaShanah is called "Keseh" because the Sefirah of Malchus is concealed, and the primary service is to build Malchus through the shofar blasts.
section.t: "Blow the shofar at the new moon, at the concealment [bakeseh] for our holiday" etc.1,
And it is explained in this regard by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Nasi of our generation
[in his maamar beginning with the words "Tik'u" of the year 57072,
(for after forty years a person stands on the understanding of his teacher3)],
that our sages, of blessed memory, said4
regarding the verse: "Which is the holiday on which the month is concealed? You must say this is Rosh HaShanah."

For "bakeseh" [means] the throne [keseh] of Hashem, where "Hashem" refers to the Sefirah of Malchus, and "keseh" means concealment; and Rosh HaShanah is called "Keseh" because on Rosh HaShanah the Sefirah of Malchus is concealed and hidden in the essential concealment, etc.
(And perhaps one may add a connection to the matter of "the holiday on which the month is concealed" simply,
for "month" simply refers to the moon,
and it is known that the moon is the Sefirah of Malchus),
and therefore the primary service of Rosh HaShanah is the building of the Sefirah of Malchus, as our sages, of blessed memory, said5
"Recite before Me [verses of] Kingship, so that you make Me King over you," etc.,
and in order to draw down the aspect of Malchus, it is through the shofar blast, as it is written, "Blow [the shofar]" etc.
